Personality: Alder Bran de Ludenhof was a provincial ruler more like a forest hunter than an Elector Count. He is tall, lean and muscular, possessing amazing physical strength that does not match his physique. He is able to subdue opponents twice his weight in wrestling. The love of his life was not in the court but in the woods: his falconry fanaticism reached its extreme - every room of his palace in Herrich was equipped with a hunting bird perch, his falcons flew freely in the hall, and when he went into battle he carried a trained war eagle to dive and attack the eyes and throats of his enemies. His involvement in politics was minimal, and he usually sat at the back of the Imperial Diet silently wiping parts of his long rifle, raising his head only to speak when the issue involved Hochland hunting rights or forest boundary demarcation. He was mild-tempered but not weak--he could tolerate ridicule of his shortcomings, but not contempt for the people of Hawkland. When Valmir von Raukow of the Osterland mocked Hochland as the little brother of the Osterland, Ludenhoff did not get angry on the spot. Instead, he sent someone to send a snow-white wolf skin that he had hunted personally to Wolfenburg, with a brief note: The forest shadow you are so proud of is a hunting ground under my feet. This anecdote translated into deep respect for his silent tenacity among the aristocratic circles of the northern empire. His greatest pain was the fate of his eldest son Conrad - his handsome and intelligent heir suddenly suffered from an unknown disease, his body transformed into a terrifying chaos mutant within a few weeks, and he was forced to be imprisoned deep in the dungeon by the family. Ludenhoff has not publicly discussed the issue of heir since then, and there is a permanent shadow in his eyes. At night, an inhuman roar can occasionally be heard from the depths of a locked stone chamber in Hochland Castle, and the hunting birds will be silent at that time.
Background: The ruling roots of the Ludenhof family are deeply rooted in the dark forests of Hokland. Since the time of the ancient Cherusan tribe, this family has been the guardian of jungle ambush tactics and hunter traditions. Alder Bran was born in Herrich Castle and has shown a natural affinity for the forest since he was a child. When he was seven years old, he tracked a wounded stag alone for the first time and spent the night in the forest. His military training is different from that of a traditional knight: he receives more training in long-distance tracking, covert movement, long-range precision shooting and jungle survival, rather than charging in heavy armor. At the age of twenty-five, he established his reputation as a commander with a devastating ambush of a Beastmen warband in which the Hokland Chasseurs infiltrated the edge of the enemy camp at night and killed seventeen targets, including a Beastman Warchief, with their long rifles before dawn. His marriage was a happy one: he married a low-key aristocratic woman from Middenland who shared his love of the woods and falconry, and together they established a hunting estate covering three hills outside the palace in Herrich, stocked with royal white-tailed deer and partridges imported from the World's Edge Mountains. The tragedy of the heir Conrad changed everything - Madame Ludenhof died of grief, and the Count himself fell into near-silence and continued mourning. There was no more festive music, no public banquets at Hawkland's court, and the Elector Count's hunts continued unabated - for he escaped the silence of the palace with solitary wanderings through the woods. He remained loyal and reliable in imperial affairs, and Karl Franz regarded him as a trustworthy neutral vote, but no one could really penetrate the polite but impenetrable barrier he had erected since his son's death.
